content.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. - **Title**: gh-715 Duplicate rework dispatch (2s apart, same SHA) — gh-1226 evidence
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-715` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:43:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:44:03Z

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

Full suite: 1512 passed, 0 failed (new gh-715 suite in `test_smAgent.js`, deployed-query guard test in `test_smGithubSource.js`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph "before: one tick, two dispatches"
    A1[issue: agent:rework] --> R1[rework-on-red-ci]
    A2[PR: agent:rework] --> R2[rework-on-label]
    R1 -->|guard keys on · gh-1226| D1[rework leg run 1]
    R2 -->|guard keys on · pr-1227| D2[rework leg run 2]
  end
  subgraph "after: one leg wins"
    B1[issue: agent:rework] -->|notPrLabels defers| R3[rework-on-label]
    B2[PR: agent:rework] --> R3
    R3 -->|cross-anchor guard + consume| D3[single rework leg]
  end
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ## 2. Diff checklist — apply to `pr_diff.txt` For every hunk, ask at least these questions: - [ ] Does the change match the ticket scope? Any scope creep? - [ ] Are new or changed public APIs contract-safe for existing callers? - [ ] Is user/external input validated, sanitized, or escaped? - [ ] Are secrets, tokens, or PATs handled safely — not logged, not interpolated into shell scripts? - [ ] Are new or modified files present under `testing/` in a non-test-automation PR? - [ ] Is dead code, unused imports, or obvious duplication introduced? - [ ] Are error paths handled, or are failures silently swallowed? - [ ] Are new dependencies justified and compatible with the existing stack? - [ ] Beyond blockers: what other maintainability, correctness, or quality improvements are visible in the changed code? ## 3. Changed-file deep read Do not review from the diff alone. Must be fixed. - **IMPORTANT** — real maintainability or correctness issue. Strongly prefer fixing before merge. - **SUGGESTION** — optional improvement, style, or future polish. Does not block merge. When in doubt, start one level higher; downgrade only after confirming the risk is negligible. ## 7. Exhaustive single-pass review Treat **every** review as the final and only review pass. The author will not get another chance to catch missed findings cheaply. - Do not defer SUGGESTION or IMPORTANT items to a later round because a BLOCKING issue exists. - After classifying all findings, re-read every changed file and ask: *"What else is improvable here?"* - Before writing outputs, verify that no obvious quality, maintainability, or correctness issue was left unreported. - Aim to surface the maximum number of actionable findings in this single iteration. ## 8. ## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

Review rules: review-after-dev issue-carrier (type issue) → dispatches anchored '· gh-N'; review-on-label is PR-anchored '· pr-N'. Review legs use the same workflow file ai-teammate.yml.

Scenario for my IMPORTANT finding: An issue gh-1226 has a review leg in flight (title '▶ review (SM) · gh-1226' — issue anchored, from review-after-dev). A human labels PR pr-1227 with agent:rework (manual rework request). rework-on-label matches; same-anchor guard checks '· pr-1227' — no run; cross-anchor guard checks '· gh-1226' — the review leg matches → suppression, skipInfo.crossAnchorActive set → label agent:rework consumed from the PR and NO rework ever dispatched. The human's manual rework request is silently dropped, and there's no re-armer for manual arms. Pre-change: the rework would have been suppressed while the review was running (no — pre-change there was no cross-anchor check, so pre-change the rework would DISPATCH alongside the review; arguably also not great but the rework would run). # Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

1. `crossAnchorKeys` — keys check: `key.indexOf('pr-') === 0` — what about keys like 'prj-...' (Jira)? Jira tickets usually like "PROJ-10" — indexOf('pr-') on lowercase key would catch "PR-..." jira tickets? Jira keys like 'PROJ-10' start with 'pro', not 'pr-'. But a Jira project key literally "PR" would produce key 'PR-123' → lowercase? The code does `String(it.key || '')` without lowercasing. GitHub keys are 'gh-1226' and 'pr-1227' presumably lowercase. Jira keys are uppercase 'PROJ-10'. So 'pr-' won't match 'PROJ-'. Edge: Jira project key 'PR' → 'PR-5' — indexOf('pr-') is case-sensitive, 'PR-5'.indexOf('pr-') = -1. OK safe.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

# Cross-anchor guard matches ANY leg kind — suppression can silently eat a rework request

The cross-anchor guard reuses `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun`, whose stub-title match is `runName.indexOf('· ' + ticketKey) !== -1` — it matches **any** active run for the opposite anchor, regardless of the leg kind in the title. Run titles carry the leg (`▶ review (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ dev (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ rework (SM) · gh-1226`), but the guard ignores it.

Combined with the new consume-on-suppression path in `processRule` (`skipInfo.crossAnchorActive` → `removeRuleLabel`), this creates a silent request-loss path:

1. Issue `gh-1226` has an active **review** (or dev / test-automation) leg, anchored `· gh-1226`.
2. A human labels PR `pr-1227` with `agent:rework` (the manual-rework rule `rework-on-label`, the only deployed rule with `consumeLabels`).
3. The same-anchor guard passes (no `· pr-1227` run), the cross-anchor guard matches the review leg → dispatch suppressed, and the `agent:rework` label is **consumed**.
4. No rework ever runs, and — unlike the machine arms covered by `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming — a manual arm has no re-armer. The request is gone.

Pre-change, a same-anchor suppression did **not** consume the label, so the rework fired once the blocking run finished; the cross-anchor check broadens the set of suppressing runs and adds consumption, turning suppression into loss.

**Suggested fix**: make the "fulfills the request" decision leg-kind-aware — e.g. have `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` accept an optional title substring (`'rework'`) so only an in-flight **rework** leg for the opposite anchor triggers the consume path (a non-rework leg should suppress-without-consume, leaving the label to re-fire on the next tick), and add a test pinning that behavior for a `▶ review (SM) · gh-…` run in flight.

# Suggestion: cross-anchor guard doubles the per-item `listWorkflowRuns` API cost

`hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` issues up to 4 `listWorkflowRuns` calls (one per queued/in_progress/waiting/pending status) — and the new cross-anchor loop runs it again for each alt key of every matching candidate item, on every tick where the rule matched. For github rules on linked issue/PR pairs this roughly doubles the SM tick's workflow-run polling for those items.

Not a problem at current scale, but if the SM tick latency or API quota ever matters, consider fetching the run list once per (workflowFile) per tick and matching all anchor tokens (same-anchor + cross-anchor) against that single snapshot.

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

{"content":"# Cross-anchor guard matches ANY leg kind — suppression can silently eat a rework request

The cross-anchor guard reuses `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun`, whose stub-title match is `runName.indexOf('· ' + ticketKey) !== -1` — it matches **any** active run for the opposite anchor, regardless of the leg kind in the title. Run titles carry the leg (`▶ review (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ dev (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ rework (SM) · gh-1226`), but the guard ignores it.

Combined with the new consume-on-suppression path in `processRule` (`skipInfo.crossAnchorActive` → `removeRuleLabel`), this creates a silent request-loss path:

1. Issue `gh-1226` has an active **review** (or dev / test-automation) leg, anchored `· gh-1226`.
2. A human labels PR `pr-1227` with `agent:rework` (the manual-rework rule `rework-on-label`, the only deployed rule with `consumeLabels`).
3. The same-anchor guard passes (no `· pr-1227` run), the cross-anchor guard matches the review leg → dispatch suppressed, and the `agent:rework` label is **consumed**.
4. No rework ever runs, and — unlike the machine arms covered by `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming — a manual arm has no re-armer. The request is gone.

Pre-change, a same-anchor suppression did **not** consume the label, so the rework fired once the blocking run finished; the cross-anchor check broadens the set of suppressing runs and adds consumption, turning suppression into loss.

**Suggested fix**: make the "fulfills the request" decision leg-kind-aware — e.g. have `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` accept an optional title substring (`'rework'`) so only an in-flight **rework** leg for the opposite anchor triggers the consume path (a non-rework leg should suppress-without-consume, leaving the label to re-fire on the next tick), and add a test pinning that behavior for a `▶ review (SM) · gh-…` run in flight.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"# Suggestion: cross-anchor guard doubles the per-item `listWorkflowRuns` API cost

`hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` issues up to 4 `listWorkflowRuns` calls (one per queued/in_progress/waiting/pending status) — and the new cross-anchor loop runs it again for each alt key of every matching candidate item, on every tick where the rule matched. For github rules on linked issue/PR pairs this roughly doubles the SM tick's workflow-run polling for those items.

Not a problem at current scale, but if the SM tick latency or API quota ever matters, consider fetching the run list once per (workflowFile) per tick and matching all anchor tokens (same-anchor + cross-anchor) against that single snapshot.

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).

- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

blocks.text:
# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
```

{"content":"# Cross-anchor guard matches ANY leg kind — suppression can silently eat a rework request

The cross-anchor guard reuses `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun`, whose stub-title match is `runName.indexOf('· ' + ticketKey) !== -1` — it matches **any** active run for the opposite anchor, regardless of the leg kind in the title. Run titles carry the leg (`▶ review (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ dev (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ rework (SM) · gh-1226`), but the guard ignores it.

Combined with the new consume-on-suppression path in `processRule` (`skipInfo.crossAnchorActive` → `removeRuleLabel`), this creates a silent request-loss path:

1. Issue `gh-1226` has an active **review** (or dev / test-automation) leg, anchored `· gh-1226`.
2. A human labels PR `pr-1227` with `agent:rework` (the manual-rework rule `rework-on-label`, the only deployed rule with `consumeLabels`).
3. The same-anchor guard passes (no `· pr-1227` run), the cross-anchor guard matches the review leg → dispatch suppressed, and the `agent:rework` label is **consumed**.
4. No rework ever runs, and — unlike the machine arms covered by `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming — a manual arm has no re-armer. The request is gone.

Pre-change, a same-anchor suppression did **not** consume the label, so the rework fired once the blocking run finished; the cross-anchor check broadens the set of suppressing runs and adds consumption, turning suppression into loss.

**Suggested fix**: make the "fulfills the request" decision leg-kind-aware — e.g. have `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` accept an optional title substring (`'rework'`) so only an in-flight **rework** leg for the opposite anchor triggers the consume path (a non-rework leg should suppress-without-consume, leaving the label to re-fire on the next tick), and add a test pinning that behavior for a `▶ review (SM) · gh-…` run in flight.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"# Suggestion: cross-anchor guard doubles the per-item `listWorkflowRuns` API cost

`hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` issues up to 4 `listWorkflowRuns` calls (one per queued/in_progress/waiting/pending status) — and the new cross-anchor loop runs it again for each alt key of every matching candidate item, on every tick where the rule matched. For github rules on linked issue/PR pairs this roughly doubles the SM tick's workflow-run polling for those items.

Not a problem at current scale, but if the SM tick latency or API quota ever matters, consider fetching the run list once per (workflowFile) per tick and matching all anchor tokens (same-anchor + cross-anchor) against that single snapshot.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment2.md"}

# Pull Request Information

- **Title**: gh-715 Duplicate rework dispatch (2s apart, same SHA) — gh-1226 evidence
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-715` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 4
- **Additions**: +254
- **Deletions**: -4
- **Created**: 2026-10-04T20:43:16Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-04T20:44:03Z

## PR Description

## What changed

Fixed the duplicate rework dispatch (gh-715): `agent:rework` armed on both the issue and the PR made one SM tick fire both rework rules 2s apart on the same head SHA. The issue-carrier rule (`rework-on-red-ci`) now defers to the PR-carrier rule via `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]`, and `triggerWorkflow` gained a cross-anchor in-flight guard (`crossAnchorKeys`) that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the other anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression so a finished run never re-fires a duplicate leg.

## Key decisions

- **Issue rule defers, PR rule wins when both armed**: `rework-on-label` is PR-anchored (#544-safe), consumes its label on dispatch; `rework-on-red-ci` deliberately keeps no `consumeLabels` (issue arm must survive dispatch for dead-letter re-fire recovery).
- **Cross-anchor guard is engine-level** (`js/smAgent.js`), not config: the PR carrier cannot read issue labels in query guards, and the guard covers the cross-tick race (PR armed later in the same tick after the issue leg dispatched).
- Suppression consumes `consumeLabels` because the in-flight leg fulfills the request; recovery stays intact via `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming while threads remain unresolved.

## How to verify

```bash
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json
```

Full suite: 1512 passed, 0 failed (new gh-715 suite in `test_smAgent.js`, deployed-query guard test in `test_smGithubSource.js`).

<details><summary>Architecture</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  subgraph "before: one tick, two dispatches"
    A1[issue: agent:rework] --> R1[rework-on-red-ci]
    A2[PR: agent:rework] --> R2[rework-on-label]
    R1 -->|guard keys on · gh-1226| D1[rework leg run 1]
    R2 -->|guard keys on · pr-1227| D2[rework leg run 2]
  end
  subgraph "after: one leg wins"
    B1[issue: agent:rework] -->|notPrLabels defers| R3[rework-on-label]
    B2[PR: agent:rework] --> R3
    R3 -->|cross-anchor guard + consume| D3[single rework leg]
  end
```

</details>

# Copilot Instructions — dmtools-agents

## Architecture

This is a **generic agents repository** (typically used as a git submodule at `agents/` inside product repos). It orchestrates AI-driven Agile delivery via [dmtools](https://github.com/nicku/dmtools) — a Java tool that provides a GraalJS runtime for agent scripts.

### Execution model

1. **SM Agent** (`sm.json` → `js/smAgent.js`) runs on a cron schedule, queries Jira via JQL rules, and dispatches specialized agents by triggering GitHub Actions workflows.
2. **Agent configs** (root `*.json` files) define individual agent jobs. Three job types exist:
   - `Teammate` — CLI-based agent (prepares context → runs AI CLI → post-processes result)
   - `JSRunner` — pure GraalJS logic executed inside dmtools (no AI CLI)
   - `TestCasesGenerator` — dmtools-native job for test case generation
3. **Project config** lives in the target repo at `.dmtools/config.js`, never here. This repo stays project-agnostic.

### Key layers

| Layer | Location | Purpose |
|-------|----------|---------|
| SM rules | `sm.json`, `sm_merge.json` | JQL-based ticket routing |
| Agent configs | root `*.json` | Job definitions (type, params, actions) |
| JS runtime scripts | `js/` | Pre/post actions, orchestration logic |
| Shared helpers | `js/common/` | SCM abstraction, Jira helpers, PR logic |
| Config system | `js/configLoader.js` + `js/config.js` | Discovery, merging, defaults |
| Prompts | `prompts/` | Markdown entry prompts for CLI agents |
| Instructions | `instructions/` | Reusable instruction packs (review, dev, rework, platform, tracker, scm) |
| Setup scripts | `setup/` | Shell scripts for CI environment setup |

## GraalJS Constraints

All `js/` runtime code executes in **dmtools GraalJS**, not Node.js.

- Use `var` declarations and plain functions (no `let`/`const`, no arrow functions, no async/await, no template literals).
- No Node.js APIs: no `fs`, `path`, `process`, `Buffer`, `child_process`, no npm packages.
- No browser APIs: no `fetch`, `window`, `document`.
- Use dmtools globals: `jira_*`, `github_*`, `ado_*`, `file_read`, `file_write`, `cli_execute_command`.
- Local `require('./module.js')` works only for files within this repo.
- Keep data structures JSON-safe.

## Running Tests

Tests run **standalone** inside dmtools GraalJS via the custom test runner. The repo is independent — no parent repo or submodule mount needed.

```bash
# Run from the dmtools-agents repo root
cd dmtools-agents

# All tests
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_all.json

# Single test suite
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_smAgent.json
dmtools run js/unit-tests/run_configLoader.json
```

Each `run_*.json` specifies which test files to load. Tests use `loadModule()` with mock injection — see `js/unit-tests/testRunner.js` for the framework API (`test()`, `suite()`, `assert.*`, `loadModule()`, `makeRequire()`).

### Writing tests for new logic

**All new JS logic must be covered by unit tests before committing.**

{"content":"# Cross-anchor guard matches ANY leg kind — suppression can silently eat a rework request

The cross-anchor guard reuses `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun`, whose stub-title match is `runName.indexOf('· ' + ticketKey) !== -1` — it matches **any** active run for the opposite anchor, regardless of the leg kind in the title. Run titles carry the leg (`▶ review (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ dev (SM) · gh-1226`, `▶ rework (SM) · gh-1226`), but the guard ignores it.

Combined with the new consume-on-suppression path in `processRule` (`skipInfo.crossAnchorActive` → `removeRuleLabel`), this creates a silent request-loss path:

1. Issue `gh-1226` has an active **review** (or dev / test-automation) leg, anchored `· gh-1226`.
2. A human labels PR `pr-1227` with `agent:rework` (the manual-rework rule `rework-on-label`, the only deployed rule with `consumeLabels`).
3. The same-anchor guard passes (no `· pr-1227` run), the cross-anchor guard matches the review leg → dispatch suppressed, and the `agent:rework` label is **consumed**.
4. No rework ever runs, and — unlike the machine arms covered by `rework-unresolved-threads` re-arming — a manual arm has no re-armer. The request is gone.

Pre-change, a same-anchor suppression did **not** consume the label, so the rework fired once the blocking run finished; the cross-anchor check broadens the set of suppressing runs and adds consumption, turning suppression into loss.

**Suggested fix**: make the "fulfills the request" decision leg-kind-aware — e.g. have `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` accept an optional title substring (`'rework'`) so only an in-flight **rework** leg for the opposite anchor triggers the consume path (a non-rework leg should suppress-without-consume, leaving the label to re-fire on the next tick), and add a test pinning that behavior for a `▶ review (SM) · gh-…` run in flight.
","path":"outputs/pr_review_comments/comment1.md"}

{"content":"# Suggestion: cross-anchor guard doubles the per-item `listWorkflowRuns` API cost

`hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` issues up to 4 `listWorkflowRuns` calls (one per queued/in_progress/waiting/pending status) — and the new cross-anchor loop runs it again for each alt key of every matching candidate item, on every tick where the rule matched. For github rules on linked issue/PR pairs this roughly doubles the SM tick's workflow-run polling for those items.

Not a problem at current scale, but if the SM tick latency or API quota ever matters, consider fetching the run list once per (workflowFile) per tick and matching all anchor tokens (same-anchor + cross-anchor) against that single snapshot.

Review complete. Verdict: **APPROVE** (0 blocking, 1 important, 1 suggestion).

## What I reviewed

PR #720 fixes gh-715 (duplicate rework dispatch 2s apart, same SHA): `rework-on-red-ci` gains `notPrLabels: ["agent:rework"]` to defer to the PR-carrier rule, and `triggerWorkflow` gains an engine-level `crossAnchorKeys` in-flight guard that suppresses a dispatch when a leg for the same issue/PR is already running under the opposite anchor — consuming the matched label on suppression. 4 files changed (+254/−4); full unit suite verified locally: **1512 passed, 0 failed**.

## Findings

1. **⚠️ IMPORTANT** (`js/smAgent.js:441-443`) — The cross-anchor guard is leg-kind-blind: `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` matches *any* active run titled `· gh-<N>` / `· pr-<N>`, including review/dev/test-automation legs. Paired with the new consume-on-suppression path, a manual `agent:rework` label on a PR can be **consumed while only a review leg is running** — the rework never dispatches and, unlike machine arms, a manual arm has no re-armer (`rework-unresolved-threads`). Pre-change, suppression never consumed the label, so the request survived until the blocking run finished. Suggested fix: only treat an in-flight **rework** leg as fulfilling the request (suppress-without-consume otherwise), plus a test pinning that behavior.

2. **💡 SUGGESTION** (`js/smAgent.js:442`) — The cross-anchor loop re-runs `hasActiveTargetWorkflowRun` (up to 4 `listWorkflowRuns` calls) per alt key per matched item per tick, doubling SM polling for linked pairs; fine at current scale, noted for future optimization.

No security issues, no CI failures, GraalJS conventions followed (`var`/plain functions), tests are meaningful and cover both carriers, the cross-tick race, and the negative case (unrelated run doesn't suppress). Ticket AC satisfied.
